Definition: properly, headship, i.e. (plural for collective) dominion
BiblicalUsage: marʼâshâh is headship, dominion, a principality, and it occurs once, in Jeremiah 13:18. There the king and queen are told to humble themselves and sit down, for their principalities shall come down, even the crown of their glory. The word is the rule that is about to fall.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe marʼâshâh warns me that crowns and principalities come down when God humbles them, and that my pride should sit down before He makes it sit.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
